text:
ana: Heads-up — thinking we should add a per-route / per-model snapshot view in the Console to show token burn, routing policy, and recent fallbacks. Quick thoughts?

matt: +1. Especially useful for quota-hit routes. Need to surface which routing policy (latency-first / cost-first) and the active model variant.

shiv: Agree. Also the filter UI needs to include model tags (quantized / fp16), traffic-split percentages, and sampled telemetry window.

ana: UX question: store these as saved queries or as ephemeral snapshots attached to a rollout? My vote: saved queries for audits, snapshots for rollouts.

evan: Implementation note: saved-queries API already supports route + model predicates; we can extend it with routing_policy and commit_sha. Example:
```
POST /api/v1/saved_queries
{
  "scope": "route:api-auth",
  "filter": {"model":"redwood-1","routing_policy":"cost-first","window":"30m"}
}
```

julie: Do we expect any existing consumers to break? We should make fields optional and provide a migration plan.

matt: +1. Console should prefer an explicit 'snapshot' field when present; otherwise reconstruct view from the latest telemetry and route config.

ana: Rollout UX: when a canary runs, surface an "active snapshot" badge vs "historical saved query". Show split percentages (e.g., canary: 10%).

deploy-bot: snapshot-service v2 deployed to staging :rocket:

shiv: For telemetry columns, include sampled p50/p95 latency, token cost delta vs baseline, and reroute events count. Add a link to per-route traces.

evan: Also add retention controls — orgs should be able to set default snapshot retention. Suggest default 90d, enterprise option longer.

ana: Sounds good. I'll draft a PRD and attach mockups. Thanks all :sparkles:
